prompt: DualReportCard implements two interfaces that both ship a default header() method. Resolve the clash by overriding header() to combine Printable.super.header() and Auditable.super.header(), and leave the other defaults alone.
explanation: When a class inherits two unrelated default methods with the same signature, Java will not pick a winner for you -- the class must override the method or it does not compile. Inside that override, InterfaceName.super.method() names exactly which inherited version you want, which is what lets you keep both instead of discarding one. The defaults that were not in conflict, render and auditLine, call header() on the object itself, so they automatically run your resolved version without any change.
hints: The compiler forces the override: one class cannot silently inherit two different default header() methods.
Qualify super with the interface name -- Printable.super.header() and Auditable.super.header() -- to reach each inherited default.
Do not touch render() or auditLine(). They already call header() on this object, so resolving header once fixes both.
